DECIDED by Sinai 2026-10-11 under the adopted model: ONE ROW PER HOUSE. Friedberg pp.111-112 documents the Warsaw Lebenzohn press across four generations — Avigdor b. Yoel ha-Kohen founds it תקע"ח/1818 (after typesetting for Nosonovitsh, and partnered with him to תקפ"א/1821); hands it to his son יואל in תרי"ב/1852 on leaving for Eretz Yisrael; Yoel prints to תרל"ג/1873; after his death it passes to HIS son יוסף, who runs it to ~תר"ס/1900, from תרל"ח with David Fridman then alone. Separately Yoel's sons Gershon and Pesach open a further press in תרט"ז/1856. The index (p.182) lists אביגדור, גרשון, יואל, יוסף and פסח לעבענזאהן together. So cluster ORG-C06526 'דפוס של ר" יוסף לעבענזאָהן' is THE SAME HOUSE as db 24 under its next proprietor, and aligns to it. The proprietor sequence stays as dated prose HERE, in the ledger, not in name_variants — per the survey (§4.3), name_variants carries only what a matcher needs. When a RiC-O-style dated-relation model is built, this prose is the source for Avigdor/Yoel/Yosef as typed successions with their dates; nothing here has to be undone to get there.

APPLIED 2026-10-10 as SPLIT. The Yiddish Book Center holdings (70 Goldfarb imprints) show Sh./S./Shelomoh Goldfarb is ONE Warsaw firm (57 items, 1900-1933) = db 50, and M. Goldfarb a SEPARATE concurrent Warsaw literary imprint (10 items, 1924-1933) with no core_db row. This 5-mention cluster mixes them: 2 mentions read ש. in their own source sentence (facs_296_r, facs_123_tr_1753936429) and belong to db 50; 2 read מ. (facs_47_r_2, facs_252_tr_1754998536) and need a new row; 1 reads ל. twice (facs_153_tr_1744279072, Lindenfeld entry, printed pp.1090-1091 vol.2) and is held for Sinai to check against the scan. Note the canonical_yiddish was the מ. form, which is why the ש. mentions were pulled in — the cluster key outvoted the mentions' own readings. SCAN-CHECK TARGET for the ל. גאָלדפאַרב reading, narrowed 2026-10-10 against the structured XML of the Lexicon itself. Across the whole corpus the initial reads: ש. 13 times (vol.2 scan pages 99, 103, 196, 344 x2, 345, 347 x3; vol.4 p.67), מ. ONCE (vol.4 scan page 51, 'מ. גאָלדפאַרב, וואַרשע, 1926'), and ל. TWICE — BOTH on vol.2 SCAN PAGE 154, both in the Lindenfeld entry (printed pp.1090-1091): 'פֿאַרלאג ל. גאָלדפאַרב, וואַרשע, 1927' and 'פער-לאג ל. גאָלדפאַרב, וואַרשא, 1928' (the second hyphenated across a line break). So the two ל readings are ADJACENT, on ONE scan page, in ONE entry — which makes a single misreading repeated by the same OCR pass across two nearby lines much likelier than a third firm; a real third Goldfarb would be expected to recur elsewhere in 7 volumes, and does not. ל and מ are not close in Yiddish print, so if the scan shows ל clearly the error is the typesetter's, not the OCR's. CHECK: volume 2, facsimile page 154 (printed 1090-1091), the two play citations in the Lindenfeld entry. The 1928 one is the better test since its line break may have confused the transcription. If ל is a misreading, the likelier original is מ (1926-28 fits M. Goldfarb's 1924-33 run) rather than ש, whose own citations cluster in 1925-27. SCAN CHECK DONE 2026-10-11 — and it OVERTURNS the OCR-slip hypothesis. ל. גאָלדפאַרב IS A REAL READING. Checked against the Yiddish Book Center's own scan of volume 2 (Internet Archive nybc201090), a transcription wholly independent of the project's Transkribus pass. The two agree: ל. appears 3 times, מ. 2 times, ש. 11 times. Two independent OCR engines do not invent the same letter in the same places. Decisively, the IA text shows a ל. occurrence the project's own transcription MISSED, in a completely different entry — the Tomashevsky play-list (IA line 2800, 'פערלאַג ל, גאָלדפאַרבּ װאַרשא 1928', Di pulishe khasene) — sitting four lines below a מ. occurrence (line 2796, 'פּערלאַג מ. גאָלדפאַרבּ װאַרשא 1926', Di neshome fun mayn folk). So ל. and מ. occur FOUR LINES APART on one page, in one list, each with its own year. A single OCR pass misreading one letter would not produce both forms in adjacent entries, and a typesetter would not either. CONCLUSION: there were THREE Warsaw Goldfarb imprints — ש. (11 mentions, 1920-1927), מ. (1926, two mentions), ל. (1927-1928, three mentions). The YBC holdings show no ל. because they hold no ל. imprint, which is a gap in one library, not evidence of absence. ACTION NEEDED: the P059 split assumed two firms; it needs a third target. The 2 ל. mentions in ORG-C04431 should go to a NEW ל. גאָלדפאַרב row rather than to db 50 or db 2817.

Skeleton scores 1.000 but WRONG, and research settles it. Riga 'Arbeterheim' (1920-23) was a front organization of the Communist Party of Latvia, registered 20 June 1920, led by Abram Ravdins with M. Shats-Anin running its publishing arm; its own branch list is Latvian only — Daugavpils, Liepaja, Rezekne — and it was banned in 1922. Warsaw 'Arbeter-heym' at Karmelicka 23 is a Bundist-milieu labour club with imprints from 1918 into the later 1920s. Rival movements, separate states, non-overlapping chronology. 'Workers' Home' was a generic label for this kind of club, which is why the names converge.

Researched online 2026-10-10 and settled: NOT a relocation. The Warsaw 'Yabne' was founded by Zalman Levitas (b. Zagare 1876), who published in Hebrew first and then Yiddish — matching the תרס"ח/1907-08 and 1910 attestations — and who, under pressure from the Polish authorities, left Warsaw for RIGA, not Palestine, remaining there as a merchant and communal figure. The Tel Aviv 'Hotsaat Yavneh' was founded in 1932 by Joshua Orenstein, has no European predecessor, and is named for the ancient academy. Zeitlin's 'Bein ha-esh ve-ha-yesha' is Tel Aviv 1957, some 45 years after the Warsaw attestations.

RESOLVED 2026-10-10: the firm is ODESSA, and the Leksikon was right all along. An earlier pass here recorded 'Vilna then Odessa' from catalogue metadata; that was WRONG and is corrected. Reading the TITLE PAGES themselves (archive.org/download/<id>/<id>_djvu.txt) shows the imprints carry TWO separate lines, and the catalogue collapsed them into one, inverting the sense: nybc204446 (1897) line 101 'בהוצאת האחים בלאמניצקי באדעססא' then line 103 'ווילנא'; nybc202364 (1909) line 95 'בהוצאת האחים בלעטניצקי. באדעססא' then line 98 'ווילנא. תרסט'; nybc214795 (1895) line 153 'הזכות נמכר לצמיתות להאחים בלעטניצקי מויס באדעססא' ('the rights were sold in perpetuity to the Bletnitski Brothers OF ODESSA') then line 162 'ווילנא'. So באדעססא names the FIRM and ווילנא names the PLACE OF PRINTING; IA's publisher field reads 'Ṿilna : ha-Aḥim Bleṭnitsḳi', which is the opposite of what the page says. NATURE: a bookshop that published and commissioned printing, never (on this evidence) a press of its own — 'פערלאג און אייגענטהום פון בוכהאנדלונג' (farlag and property of the bookshop), 'בית מסחר הספרים' (book-trading house); the 1911 play was printed at Bialik & Borishkin's shop in Odessa. Business model: buying rights outright and reissuing popular Yiddish fiction, which is why its name sits over books printed in other cities. ACTIVITY c.1878-1918, Warsaw -> Odessa; the 1878 Warsaw imprint names the brothers as Heym (Chaim) and Perets Bletnitski, though that is a single source and early enough that the 1900s firm may be sons or younger brothers. Published Shomer and Linetzky, Yiddish drama and operetta (the theatrical connection: Lebedig un lustig 1914, Di hayrat-komedye 1911, Madam Freylein), Klausner's 4-volume Historiyah Yisreelit (1915), a Hebrew children's library after I. B. Levner's death, and a 1918 Haggadah. MINT AS ONE ORG seated in ODESSA — not Vilna — with both clusters attached. OPEN: whether a Vilna shopfront ever existed. On this evidence no; the Leksikon's own Shomer bibliography lists 'Vilna: Bletnitski' but was likely compiled from these same two-line title pages, so it is probably the same error propagating, not independent evidence. An Odessa or Vilna commercial register would settle it.

MODELLING QUESTION raised by Sinai 2026-10-10: how to represent successive (and non-successive) owners of a publishing dynasty. PROPOSAL, built on precedent already in this DB rather than a new scheme. (1) SUCCESSION = ONE ORG. The PI ruled on exactly this shape for theatre families (Kaminski/Kaminska, 2026-06-02): 'though Kaminski is the father and Kaminska wife and then daughter... we would like to preserve the continuity of the family in the entity', and 6 rows were merged into db 147. A press passing father to son is the same continuity, so Lebenzohn — Avigdor (1818) -> Yoel (1852) -> Yosef (to ~1900) — is ONE org, canonically db 24, with each proprietor's form in name_variants and the successions in the notes. The alternative, a row per proprietor, would fragment one imprint across three ids and make every cluster align ambiguous. (2) CONCURRENT RELATIVES = SEPARATE ORGS. Where two family members run imprints AT THE SAME TIME they are different businesses: Sh. Goldfarb (1900-1933) and M. Goldfarb (1924-1933) overlap for a decade, so they are two rows (P059/P156). The test is chronological overlap, not surname. (3) PARTNERSHIPS STAY SEPARATE, by the same memory's rule that conjunction entities are distinct — but a partnership PHASE of one continuing firm is not a conjunction: Baumritter 1891-95 'and his son-in-law Ganshar' is db 157 during those years (P057), not a fourth org. (4) BRANCHES use parent_db_id, which the DB already does for Forverts New York/Chicago/Philadelphia/Detroit under db 249. A firm that MOVED (Bletnitski, Warsaw->Odessa) is one row with the later seat in address and the earlier noted, NOT a parent/child pair — parent_db_id is for simultaneous branches. OPEN FOR SINAI: whether the per-proprietor detail should be carried in name_variants (cheap, lossy) or whether a dynasty deserves rows with parent_db_id pointing at the house (costlier, queryable). Only 10 rows use parent_db_id today, all of them place-branches, so extending it to succession would be a new convention and should be a deliberate choice.
